quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2025 results and end-market mix: net sales were $1,482,073 thousand for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 versus $1,311,120 thousand in 2024 (+13.0%); gross profit was 31.2% of net sales versus 33.2%. Computing - whose applications the 10-K lists as including notebooks, solid state and hard disk drives, artificial intelligence servers, storage, cloud computing and data center - rose to 27% of product revenue in 2025 from 25% in 2024 and 23% in 2023; industrial was 23%, automotive 19%, consumer 18% and communications 13% (5G networks, routers, switches, fiber optics).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 net sales $1,482,073 thousand (+13.0% from $1,311,120 thousand); gross margin 31.2% (33.2%); computing 27% of product revenue (25% in 2024, 23% in 2023)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K customer concentration and channel (customers not named): direct sales and EMS customers together accounted for 35% of net sales in 2025 (37% in 2024, 32% in 2023); direct sales were $522,368 thousand and distributor sales $959,705 thousand in 2025. Two customers each accounted for 10% or more of net sales - Customer 1 with $182,314 thousand and Customer 2 with $157,735 thousand in 2025 - and both are broad-based distributors serving thousands of customers. In 2025 approximately 45% of total sales were shipped to customers in China.
quarterly_data.figure: direct + EMS 35% of net sales (37%, 32%); direct sales $522,368 thousand, distributor sales $959,705 thousand; Customer 1 $182,314 thousand, Customer 2 $157,735 thousand (distributors); approximately 45% shipped to China

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K manufacturing footprint, capex and commitments: Diodes operates wafer fabrication facilities in China, Great Britain, Taiwan and the United States and assembly and test facilities in China, Taiwan and Germany; notwithstanding its use of third-party capacity, most production requirements are met by its own facilities (hybrid manufacturing model). SPFAB in South Portland, Maine (acquired from onsemi in June 2022) provides additional 200mm wafer capacity for analog products, and GFAB in Greenock, Scotland (acquired from Texas Instruments in 2019) is a 200mm wafer fab. Cash capital expenditures were approximately $78.4 million in 2025 (5.3% of net sales) versus $73.0 million in 2024, primarily for manufacturing expansion in assembly/test and wafer fabrication; over the long term the company expects capex within its 5% to 9% of net sales target model. At December 31, 2025 it had non-cancelable capex purchase contracts of approximately $51.9 million, primarily for manufacturing equipment, and a commitment to purchase approximately $52.4 million of wafers scheduled through 2031.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex approximately $78.4 million (5.3% of net sales; $73.0 million in 2024); target 5% to 9% of net sales; equipment purchase contracts approximately $51.9 million; wafer purchase commitment approximately $52.4 million through 2031

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure - Supplier Nuvoton (related party): Diodes purchases wafers from Nuvoton Technology Corporation for use in its production process and has an agreement to purchase approximately $3.1 million of wafers from Nuvoton that ends in the second quarter of 2027; purchases from Nuvoton were $6,454 thousand in 2025 ($7,076 thousand in 2024). Related party Keylink, a 5% joint venture partner in the Shanghai assembly and test facilities, leases those manufacturing facilities to Diodes' China subsidiaries and performs subcontracted metal plating and environmental services.
quarterly_data.figure: Nuvoton wafer purchase agreement approximately $3.1 million ending Q2 2027; Nuvoton purchases $6,454 thousand in 2025 ($7,076 thousand in 2024)
